summary: Mendocino County lookout planned in 1929, a station reported in 1930, and a 60-foot steel tower erected by CCC crews in 1935; listed as removed with no date, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: steel tower with concrete footings (1935 plan; 1956 survey description)
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it removed with no date; firelookout.org lists it as gone; no source describes the site now

staffing.status: lookout man planned for 1929; observer to go on duty in 1930; no later staffing found

July 1930 item says a station had just been built at the head of the Gualala River; not clear whether it was the same structure as the 1935 tower
July 1930 item says an observer would go on duty at the station
June 1935 item announced a 60-foot-high steel tower; a July 1935 item says a CCC crew was sent to erect it, and an August 1935 item says CCC camp workers were building it

Survey disk recovered in good condition; the recovery note does not describe the tower

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A July 1930 item calls a station just built at the head of the Gualala River; a June 1935 item announces a 60-foot steel tower to be built, and July and August 1935 items describe CCC crews erecting or building it. The sources do not say whether these were one structure or two, so the story reports both without joining them.

Forest Lookouts names the California Department of Forestry and the January 1929 item refers to the state Division of Forestry, while the 1938 survey mark is described as monumented by the USFS. The sources do not explain the difference; the story gives the state agency and notes the mark.

notes_for_editor: Six newspaper items quoted by Forest Lookouts, the 1956 to 1964 survey datasheet, and one index row. The height_m of 18.3 comes from a June 1935 plan for a 60-foot tower and was not measured; the record height matches it. Name: the 1929 items say Gualala Peak, while the 1930 and 1935 items name only the station at the head of the Gualala River or the Gualala lookout; the index and brief say Gualala Mountain. Removal date unknown. The datasheet's last recovery is 1964 and does not describe the tower. Current public access is unknown; the 1956 route is historical. The NGS stamp reads ELEVATION 2187 FEET but the story does not use it, since the source is a survey mark, not a lookout record.
